purpose: Explain owning-load RSS; diagnostic runs, not replacements for the repeated speed benchmark.
environment: Same GCC 13.3 Linux x86_64 Release library and native-t1 datasets as optimized-threading.json; OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; sequential processes.
method: Fresh process per case; process RSS from /proc/self/statm; peak RSS from getrusage.
Full load into an initially empty destination; no legacy input generation, conversion or digest verification.

Query/match/evidence/score vector capacities and heap string capacities counted through public accessors; metadata counts are a lower bound using occupied entries and separate string objects, excluding vector spare capacity and allocator overhead.
The PSM accounting excludes run/protein/inference objects, runtime libraries, Arrow allocations and allocator overhead. Empty-option counts are counts, not bytes.
malloc_trim is a diagnostic only; it is not added to production code and cannot release live objects or non-glibc allocator caches.
Scan retains no callback records and uses default full projection, buffering and non-strict ID-uniqueness option; it does not load protein inference. Both counters equal 1,000,000.
The 1,000-run generated workload contains 200 protein hits per run versus 200 total in the single-run case, so its additional memory is not solely run-descriptor overhead.

reproduction.build: Compile the diagnostic_source with the includes/link flags of IdentificationDataLegacyBenchmark, using -O3 -DNDEBUG -std=c++23. The probe additionally uses Linux /proc and glibc malloc diagnostics.
